newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pepsico's NZ Restaurant Brands makes tasty debut.
newsitem.headline: Pepsico's NZ Restaurant Brands makes tasty debut.

text.p: Shares in Restaurant Brands New Zealand Ltd, floated for NZ$187 million ($130 million) on Wednesday, soared at their market debut amid strong local and overseas interest.
The Pepsico Inc unit's flotation of 85 million shares had been three times oversubscribed and the shares were placed at the top of a NZ$1.80-$2.20 prospectus range, its promoters said.
Having opened up 20 cents at NZ$2.40 on the New Zealand Stock Exchange the shares closed up a net 26 cents at $2.46.

Restaurant Brands was formed earlier this year to take over the KFC and Pizza Hut restaurant franchise operations of Pepsico in New Zealand, as part of a wider international process to help Pepsico exit direct ownership of the restaurant business.
The offer was oversubscribed by about 300 percent with tenders received for about 338 million shares.
Gross proceeds from the 85 million shares would therefore be about NZ$187 million.
As a result of the oversubscription, members of the New Zealand public who had not received firm allocations would be limited to a maximum of 1,000 shares each, RB said.
Tim Snedden at brokers ANZ Securities said it was a healthy debut for the stock, particularly given the flat market overall.
"It's indicative of a pretty successful float," he said.
"When you get a premium like that there is plenty of stagging (profit-taking) margin in there and it's not surprising to see a few people turn them over," Snedden added.
Other brokers said they had fielded many enquiries from retail clients throughout the day and about 8.3 million shares changed hands during the day.
The overall market ended up with the NZ Top 40 index rising 7.61 points to 2,357.03 in turnover worth nearly NZ$86 million.
After allocation of shares, Restaurant Brands is expected to have about 15,000 shareholders with about 61 percent of its shares held by New Zealand retail and institutional investors.
Analysts had predicted that the issue would be well- supported by international investors, with U.S. institutions expected to take a healthy interest in the new company. (US$=NZ$1.44)
